methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective biomarker analysis in two phase III RCTs (CONTINUUM/DIPPER) with discovery and validation design. Machine learning classifier trained and validated on independent cohort with clear methodology. Stratified Cox models and interaction testing appropriately applied. Minor limitation: exploratory nature of metabolic subtyping without pre-specification, though internal validation across clustering algorithms performed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Secondary biomarker analysis of two phase III RCTs in locally-advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma with robust clinical endpoints (EFS). Findings directly applicable to treatment selection for anti-PD-1 therapy in defined patient population. Demonstrates differential treatment benefit across metabolic subtypes with significant interaction (P=0.0074), supporting clinical translation. LoE 2b reflects cohort design from RCT data.

reporting_quality.justification: Manuscript follows REMARK guideline requirements for biomarker studies with comprehensive methods, flow diagrams, and statistical approaches detailed. Clear reporting of discovery/validation approach, clustering methods, and classifier performance. Supplementary methods referenced (Data Supplement). No explicit statement of data availability or code sharing; web-based tool mentioned but deposition not confirmed.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies metabolism-based subtypes as predictive biomarker for immunotherapy, addressing documented gap in NPC biomarker landscape. First metabolic classifier for EFS benefit prediction in this disease. However, builds on known metabolic reprogramming principles and previous immune subtyping from same group; novelty is in application and validation rather than conceptual innovation.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear hypothesis, comprehensive results, and thoughtful discussion. Figures and tables effectively communicate metabolic pathway activities and treatment interactions. Methods clearly detailed. Discussion appropriately addresses limitations including generalizability to non-endemic regions and requirement for further mechanism studies.

key_strengths: Dual-cohort discovery-validation design in large phase III RCTs with 407 patients total
Robust machine learning classifier with >90% accuracy, amenable to clinical translation via web-based tool
Metabolic subtypes demonstrate independent predictive value beyond PD-L1, HER2, and TMB
Mechanistic insights via network analysis (CARNIVAL) linking SIX1/AKT pathway to treatment response
Addresses critical unmet need: only 15% of patients derive benefit from anti-PD-1; this classifier identifies responders
key_concerns: Classifier developed in endemic-region population; generalizability to non-endemic regions unknown
Predictive value shown for anti-PD-1 but not yet tested with other immunotherapies
MS1 subtype enrichment in CONTINUUM (63%) limits representation of other subtypes in training data
Mechanistic link between metabolic signatures and drug response requires functional validation
External validation limited to one additional cohort (Yeo et al); prospective validation pending
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous biomarker study with dual-cohort design, mechanistic rationale, and clinical applicability. Substantial methodological rigor and clear clinical relevance warrant consideration for high-tier venue, though mechanism details need experimental validation for Tier 1 acceptance. Minor revisions needed for mechanistic clarity and prospective validation discussion.
